key_insight: 3D Cartesian PDE solvers can be reduced exactly to repeated 1D line solves via tensor-product/Kronecker factorization, so the 3D operator is never assembled in memory.
engineering_relevance: This turns many CFD and PDE kernels into bandwidth-efficient, parallelizable line operations with linear complexity in problem size and major savings in storage.
method: Derive Kronecker-product forms for finite differences, compact schemes, Galerkin, spline/IGA, collocation, ADI, and separable Poisson/Helmholtz solvers.
Use multi-right-hand-side reshaping to execute sweeps as batched line kernels; exploit BLAS-3 when dense and banded/stencil kernels otherwise.
Apply sum factorization and pencil decomposition to keep high-order quadrature and distributed-memory data movement efficient.
evidence_signal: The abstract argues analytically that for fixed stencil width or polynomial degree the compute cost is O(N), storage is O(Nx+Ny+Nz) up to bandwidth factors, and the line kernels are embarrassingly parallel.
watch_item: Performance depends on keeping line directions contiguous and on the cost of communication/reshaping; high-order methods can still suffer if sum factorization or pencil layout is not implemented carefully.
paper_title: No 3D Matrices: A Unified Tensor-Product View of Matrix-Free Cartesian PDE Solvers
